message.content:
Sure! Use the `maxsplit` argument of `str.split()` so it only splits on the first `=`:

```python
temp = "hello=good="

# Split only once (maxsplit=1)
parts = temp.split('=', 1)

print(parts)   # → ['hello', 'good=']
```

`maxsplit=1` tells Python to perform at most one split, leaving the rest of the string intact. This gives you exactly `["hello", "good="]`.
